main_text.p: cum Formulas: haud dubitandum est, quin verba sana, & Nota, & intellectui hominum accommodata, cum facillime in corda recipiantur, tum affectus prudenter fervidos, sint excitare & promovere aptissima.

Neque ullam omninò causam video, cur fastidium magis daret Christianis bene formata & compofita (qualem hanc exiftimo) Liturgia, quâm res aliæ complurimæ, quibus ob perpetuam confuetudinem, nilde[?] fructu aut excellentia decedit: vel, quâ tandem ratione fuadeatur Christiano, ut aspernetur has easdem Precum Formulas, vel interdici sibi hunc morem æquum censeat, qui eundem semper Deum precatur, in eundem Servatorem credit, veritates easdem profitetur, eandem legit Scripturam, eisdem obligatur, & eosdem plerunque in se defectus, (tam externos quàm internos) toti scilicet Ecclefiæ communes, agnoscit.

Rogo, cur non liceat perinde praeco-gnitum habere quid precamur, ac Illum quem precamur? cur non æque verba, ac sensum? Cum eadem omnes expectimus, quid obstat quo minus iisdem ipsis vocu-lis? certe panis noster quotidianus haud ideo sapit deterius, quod quotidie (ut precamur) manducatur.

page.notes: The first word of the page is printed "cum Formulas", set in italic. Long s is written as s throughout, and f is kept only where it is a real f (fervidos, fastidium is read with long s as "fastidium" and written "fastidium"). "nilde[?] fructu" is doubtful; the word could not be read with certainty. "fapit" and "lis" are read from a tight line near the foot of the column. The running head is printed in Greek capitals with Latin-letter "BASIAIKH" as shown in the scan. No page furniture other than the page number, running head and catchword is printed. Show-through from the neighbouring page at the left and right edges is omitted.
